title: pangrowth workflow parameters
description: Estimate pangenome growth, core size, and Hill-number diversity from a collection of genomes.

input.description: Genome folder(s), archive(s), or FASTA list file(s)
input.help_text: Select one file or folder. In Raw mode, several input paths can be separated by commas or whitespace, and a wildcard pattern can match several inputs (for example s3://BUCKET/pangenomes/*.txt). Commas are recommended; input paths cannot themselves contain commas or whitespace. Types are detected automatically: a folder contributes FASTA files directly inside it (subfolders are ignored), .txt and .list files contain one FASTA path per line, and .zip, .tar.gz, and .tgz files are genome archives. Every folder or selected file defines one pangenome. At least three genomes are required per pangenome.

outdir.help_text: Directory in which results are grouped by pangenome. Runs with multiple inputs also contain an all/ folder with combined plots.

analysis.title: Analysis Parameters
analysis.description: Parameters controlling k-mer counting and the reported analyses.

kmer.help_text: Length of nucleotide k-mers used to represent the genomes. Smaller values may be appropriate for short or heterogeneous sequences.

minimum_count.help_text: A k-mer must occur at least this many times within a genome to be considered present. Values above one can reduce sequencing-error noise in read data.

quorum.help_text: Minimum fraction of genomes in which an item must occur to count toward the quorum core. The workflow also computes the strict core separately.

canonical.help_text: Treat each k-mer and its reverse complement as the same item. This is recommended for ordinary nucleotide genome data.

expert.title: Expert Parameters
expert.description: Low-level counting and Hill-number sampling settings.

suffix_size.help_text: Number of suffix bits used to partition the k-mer hashtable. A value of 10 creates 2^10 = 1,024 partitions; it does not mean 10 nucleotide characters. Larger values create more partitions and have a substantial memory overhead.

hill_points.help_text: Number of interpolation and extrapolation sample points. Use 0 to report every point.
